content.overview: Section 109 regulates when a poll may or must be ordered at a general meeting, who may demand it, when it is taken, how it is scrutinised, and that the poll result is the decision of the meeting on the resolution. Before or on the declaration of the result of voting on any resolution on a show of hands, a poll may be ordered by the Chairman on his own motion and shall be ordered on a valid demand by the members the section names.
content.glance: A poll may be ordered by the Chairman on his own motion, and must be ordered on a valid demand by the members specified in section 109. Timing, scrutinisers, manner and the conclusive effect of the poll result are also governed by the section.
content.study:
## Section 109 — demand for poll

**Subsection (1): power and duty to order a poll.** Before or on the declaration of the result of the voting on any resolution on a show of hands, a poll may be ordered to be taken by the Chairman of the meeting on his own motion, and shall be ordered to be taken by him on a demand made in that behalf—
- (a) in the case of a company having a share capital, by the members present in person or by proxy, where allowed, and having not less than one-tenth of the total voting power or holding shares on which an aggregate sum of not less than five lakh rupees or such higher amount as may be prescribed has been paid-up; and
- (b) in the case of any other company, by any member or members present in person or by proxy, where allowed, and having not less than one-tenth of the total voting power.

**Subsection (2): withdrawal.** The demand for a poll may be withdrawn at any time by the persons who made the demand.

**Subsection (3): forthwith polls.** A poll demanded for adjournment of the meeting or appointment of Chairman of the meeting shall be taken forthwith.

**Subsection (4): other polls — 48-hour outer limit.** A poll demanded on any question other than adjournment of the meeting or appointment of Chairman shall be taken at such time, not being later than forty-eight hours from the time when the demand was made, as the Chairman of the meeting may direct.

**Subsection (5): scrutinisers.** Where a poll is to be taken, the Chairman of the meeting shall appoint such number of persons, as he deems necessary, to scrutinise the poll process and votes given on the poll and to report thereon to him in the manner as may be prescribed.

**Subsection (6): manner of the poll.** Subject to the provisions of this section, the Chairman of the meeting shall have power to regulate the manner in which the poll shall be taken.

**Subsection (7): result.** The result of the poll shall be deemed to be the decision of the meeting on the resolution on which the poll was taken.

## Apply the provision
- Identify whether the company has a share capital (clause (a)) or not (clause (b)), and whether the demand meets the statutory threshold.
- Check timing: appointment of Chairman or adjournment → forthwith; any other question → within 48 hours as the Chairman directs.
- Distinguish the Chairman's own motion from a member demand, and note that a demand may be withdrawn under subsection (2).
- Read with section 107 (show of hands, which section 109 displaces once a poll is ordered) and section 108 (electronic voting). Private-company application may be modified by articles under the section 462 framework; that is a separate current-law check.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Subsection (1): when a poll may or must be ordered
sections.body: Before or on the declaration of the result of voting on a show of hands, the Chairman may order a poll on his own motion and shall order a poll on a demand by the members specified in clause (a) (company with share capital) or clause (b) (any other company).

sections.heading: Subsections (2)–(4): withdrawal and timing
sections.body: A demand may be withdrawn by those who made it. A poll on appointment of Chairman or adjournment is taken forthwith. Any other poll is taken within forty-eight hours as the Chairman directs.

sections.heading: Subsections (5)–(7): scrutinisers, manner and result
sections.body: The Chairman appoints scrutinisers as prescribed, regulates the manner of the poll, and the poll result is deemed to be the decision of the meeting on that resolution.

examples.title: Valid demand by members with share capital
examples.body: In a company with share capital, members present in person or by proxy holding not less than one-tenth of the total voting power demand a poll before the show-of-hands result is declared. The Chairman must order the poll. This is an educational illustration, not advice about a real meeting.

examples.title: Poll on adjournment taken forthwith
examples.body: A poll is demanded on a motion to adjourn the meeting. Under subsection (3) that poll is taken forthwith, not within the 48-hour window that applies to other questions. This is an educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Members holding shares on which an aggregate of four lakh rupees has been paid up demand a poll in a company with share capital. They do not hold one-tenth of the total voting power. Is the demand valid under section 109(1)(a)?
hypotheticals.analysis: Clause (a) requires either not less than one-tenth of the total voting power or holding shares on which an aggregate sum of not less than five lakh rupees (or such higher amount as may be prescribed) has been paid-up. Four lakh does not meet the paid-up limb, and the voting-power limb is not met on the stated facts. The demand is not valid under subsection (1)(a) on those facts alone. Confirm the exact holdings and any prescribed higher amount.

hypotheticals.question: A poll is demanded on an ordinary resolution (not adjournment or appointment of Chairman). The Chairman directs that it be taken three days later. Is that consistent with section 109(4)?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Subsection (4) requires that such a poll be taken at a time not later than forty-eight hours from the demand, as the Chairman directs. Three days exceeds that outer limit.

misconceptions.trap: Treating any single member's demand as sufficient in a company with share capital.
misconceptions.correction: Clause (a) requires members present in person or by proxy having not less than one-tenth of the total voting power, or holding shares on which an aggregate of not less than five lakh rupees (or higher prescribed amount) has been paid-up.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every poll may be deferred for up to 48 hours.
misconceptions.correction: A poll on appointment of Chairman or adjournment must be taken forthwith under subsection (3). The 48-hour outer limit in subsection (4) applies only to other questions.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the show-of-hands declaration as still conclusive after a valid poll is ordered.
misconceptions.correction: Once a poll is ordered under section 109, the poll result is deemed to be the decision of the meeting on that resolution (subsection (7)); the show-of-hands result does not stand.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 109 regulate?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 109 regulates when a poll may or must be ordered (Chairman motion or valid member demand), the demand thresholds for companies with and without share capital, withdrawal of the demand, timing (forthwith for Chairman/adjournment; within 48 hours otherwise), appointment of scrutinisers, the Chairman's power over manner, and that the poll result is the decision of the meeting on the resolution.

Companies Act, 2013, sections 107 and 108, where show of hands or electronic voting is relevant
examTips: State both demand limbs in subsection (1)(a): voting power and paid-up amount.
Separate forthwith polls (Chairman/adjournment) from the 48-hour outer limit.
End with subsection (7): poll result is the decision of the meeting.
revisionPoints: Subsection (1): Chairman may order a poll on his own motion and must order on a valid demand (1/10 voting power or ₹5 lakh paid-up for share-capital companies; 1/10 voting power otherwise).
Subsection (3): poll on appointment of Chairman or adjournment — forthwith.
Subsection (4): other polls — not later than 48 hours.
Subsection (7): poll result is deemed the decision of the meeting.
